attempts.prompt:
Use case: compositing. Image1 is the sole authority for clothing, pose, hair, expression, light, and crop. Image2 provides only the mascot identity and anatomy. Transform the human anatomy into a smooth golden-yellow compact near-round mascot head and body with green-ringed black eyes and a source-matching mouth. Preserve the actual bareheaded state with short neatly side-parted dark brown hair and real brow hair. Maintain the clean upper lip and chin with no moustache, beard, or spectacles, and keep the serious closed mouth and mild image-left angle. Retain the dark navy ceremonial closed upright-collar uniform with broad gold high collar, ornate gold shoulder epaulettes, diagonal gold chain or cord, and the exact original small-card green sash across the chest with only source-visible pale, gold, and red decoration regions. Do not copy a different outfit. Ensure the rounded chin immediately meets the raised and broadened existing neckline with a very short broad neck transition and minimal throat exposure. Avoid separate yellow neck shafts, pointed V funnels, pinched collars, neck rolls, floating collars, clipping, or cream belly bibs. Preserve the actual open or closed garment and fastening with coherent front and rear collar overlap and contact shadows. Retain the complete tilted dark frame and opaque blue-grey photographic backing in its actual source color. The original source has no paper note, pin, or attachment, so do not add any cream note or foreground attachment. All solid surfaces must remain opaque with alpha only outside the complete card silhouette. Do not invent insignia, text, or accessories. Keep fine primary details understated where indistinct.
FINAL EXACT SOURCE REQUIREMENT: Actual framed formal bust with NO PAPER NOTE OR OTHER FOREGROUND ATTACHMENT. BAREHEADED, short neatly side-parted DARK BROWN hair, real brow HAIR, clean upper lip/chin with no moustache or beard or spectacles, serious CLOSED mouth, mild IMAGE-LEFT angle. DARK NAVY ceremonial CLOSED upright-collar uniform with broad GOLD high collar, ornate GOLD shoulder epaulettes, diagonal GOLD chain/cord and actual GREEN sash across chest plus only source-visible pale/gold/red decoration regions. Preserve exact original small-card green sash and arrangement; do not copy a different outfit from elsewhere. Original opaque BLUE/GREY photographic backing and dark tilted frame remain complete, genuine alpha only outside frame. DO NOT ADD A CREAM NOTE, PIN OR ATTACHMENT.
Retain exact primary head angle, expression, cap shape, real hair and visible clothing/decoration areas. One compact near-round yellow mascot head with a clearly ROUNDED short chin immediately contacting raised broad collar, no V-shaped lower-face funnel or yellow shaft. Preserve green-ringed black mascot eyes and real eyebrow HAIR. Do not copy human long neck or angular jaw into mascot anatomy; fit original neckline around compact round head. Preserve actual dark solid cloth and photographic backing opacity. Tiny ambiguous features remain understated; no new badge engraving or decoration outside actually exposed source regions. Preserve an attached note ONLY where actually present; otherwise do not invent one. Image1 exact original card; Image2 mascot identity/anatomy only.
Output alpha: genuine transparent RGBA ONLY OUTSIDE the complete original framed portrait silhouette. The photographic BACKING INSIDE the frame is a required OPAQUE surface: preserve its original background color and texture behind the character all the way to the inner frame rim. Never turn the gaps between frame and character into transparent holes or a window. Keep the actual frame angle and rim. Preserve an overlapping paper note, pin or other attachment ONLY when actually visible in this exact source; otherwise do not invent one. Do not invent a new backdrop outside the whole card. Retain source clothing, hair, headgear, lighting and crop at full generated resolution. All originally OPAQUE subject surfaces must remain FULLY OPAQUE (alpha 255): yellow head/body, hair, beard, dark or black clothing, coat lapels, collar, tie, buttons and decorations. Dark cloth is colored material, not transparent background. Never fade garment interiors into semi-transparent patches, holes, white haze or see-through fabric. Keep any genuine source outer-edge alpha falloff only at that actual exterior boundary; preserve actual source transparency rather than making the subject itself translucent.
